script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

MRS. JENKINS (mid 40s), a warm, nurturing woman, stands at the kitchen counter, sipping coffee. She looks out the window and sees her neighbor, MR. GARCIA (early 50s), struggling to load groceries into his car.

MRS. JENKINS
(calling out)
Hi, Jose! Let me help you with that.

INT. GARCIA LIVING ROOM - LATER

Mrs. Jenkins carries in a bag of groceries and sets it down on the coffee table. Mr. Garcia's young daughter, LUCY (8), runs up to her.

LUCY
(excitedly)
Mrs. Jenkins, you're here! I made you a picture!

She hands Mrs. Jenkins a colorful drawing of a sunflower. Mrs. Jenkins smiles, genuinely touched.

MRS. JENKINS
(praising)
It's beautiful, Lucy. I'll hang it up in my kitchen.

INT. SCHOOL HALLWAY - DAY

Mrs. Jenkins walks her own son, MIKE (10), to his classroom. They pass Lucy, who is sitting on the floor with a group of children, drawing.

MIKE
(smiling)
Hi, Lucy.

LUCY
(smiling back)
Hi, Mike.

INT. JENKINS KITCHEN - DINNER

The Jenkins family sits down for dinner. Mrs. Jenkins serves tacos, a favorite of Mr. Garcia's. He stops by to thank them and shares a story about Lucy's day at school.

MR. GARCIA
(laughing)
And then, she drew a picture of the solar system for the class. The teacher was amazed!

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Mrs. Jenkins and Mr. Garcia sit in comfortable chairs, talking. They discuss their families, their dreams, and their shared love for the community.

MR. GARCIA
(looking at Mrs. Jenkins)
You know, Mary, I've lived here for a long time, but I've never had a friend like you.

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling)
And I feel the same way about you, Jose.

INT. PARK - DAY

Mrs. Jenkins and Mr. Garcia sit on a bench, feeding the ducks. Lucy rides her bike up to them, her face filled with excitement.

LUCY
Look what I made!

She shows them a handmade book. Mrs. Jenkins and Mr. Garcia praise her work and share stories from their childhoods.

INT. JENKINS KITCHEN - MORNING

Mrs. Jenkins makes pancakes for Lucy, who eagerly helps. They sit down to enjoy their breakfast together.

LUCY
(looking at Mrs. Jenkins)
I'm glad you're my friend, Mrs. Jenkins.

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling)
And I'm glad you're mine, Lucy.

INT. GARCIA LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Mrs. Jenkins and Mr. Garcia sit on the couch, watching their children play together. They share a look of contentment, knowing that their friendship has brought joy to not only their lives but also those of their children.

MR. GARCIA
(whispering)
To new beginnings and lasting friendships.

MRS. JENKINS
(agrees)
Here, here.

FADE OUT.
